messages:
sara: Customer (tenant `acme-pay`) reports repeated 503s from hosted inference streaming endpoints starting ~2026-01-28T09:10Z. They say SDK v1.4.1 spawns ~120 concurrent streams and sees `upstream: 503` + occasional `RST_STREAM`. Request-id sample: r-3f9a7.

ops-bot: [deploy-bot] no deploys to prod in last 2h. alert: edge-gw-3 connection queue depth spike @ 09:09-09:12 UTC.

michael: Can you paste a minimal repro (curl or SDK loop) and the X-Redwood-Request-Id header values/log snippets? Also confirm if traffic is HTTP/2 (likely) and if they use our default SDK connection pooling.

sara: Repro they provided (sanitized):
```bash
TOKEN=redacted
for i in $(seq 1 120); do
  curl -s -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \\n    -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \\n    -H "X-Redwood-Client: acme-pay-test" \\n    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream/generate \\n    -d '{"model":"redwood-k-lite","input":"short prompt"}' &
done; wait
```
They also attached a short edge log: `edge-gw-3 | conn_count=1024 queue_len=230 drop=45 upstream=503 rst_stream=12`.

raj: Looks like connection-pool saturation on our HTTP/2 fronting layer. Symptoms: high concurrent short-lived streams, queue grows, once queue > threshold we return 503 (fail-fast to protect backends). The `RST_STREAM` count suggests clients closing mid-stream. Likely root cause: client concurrency + keepalive/idle mismatch resulting in many ephemeral h2 streams instead of reusing persistent connections.

michael: Short-term remediation options:
- Ask customer to throttle to <= 40 concurrent streams (works immediately).
- Push SDK patch (1.4.3) that enables persistent connection reuse by default for stream workloads (backport PR ready).
- Apply ingress smoothing for tenant `acme-pay` to cap burst concurrency at 80 while we roll a fix.

sara: I told the customer to throttle to 50 and try SDK 1.4.3 prerelease. They said throttling helped (fewer 503s) and will test the prerelease. I applied a temporary tenant-level smoothing policy (burst cap 80, steady 40) at 09:30 UTC.

julie: Created tracking ticket INFRA-4581 for permanent fix: increase per-node h2 conn limit, tune queue depth and add smarter tenant-level backpressure. Assigned to raj + michael, ETA for canary next week. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INFRA-4581

raj: For repro we validated locally by running the same curl loop against a staging edge with conn_limit=1024. When seq>80 we see queue climb then 503s. Repro snippet: 
```text
edge-staging$ tail -n50 edge.log | grep queue_len
2026-01-28T09:11:02Z queue_len=45 conn_count=980
2026-01-28T09:11:22Z queue_len=210 conn_count=1024 drop=12 upstream=503
```
Permanent fix plan: bump per-node limit + change default SDK to pooled connections for streaming, and add a telemetry alert on tenant burst queueing.

michael: I'll schedule the canary change to increase conn limit + staging verification tomorrow morning, and cut the backport release for SDK 1.4.3 today.

sara: Customer update posted: "We've applied a temporary smoothing policy and suggested upgrading to SDK 1.4.3; please throttle concurrent streams to 50 while we validate a permanent fix. We'll follow up when the canary is live." They replied :thumbsup:.

julie: Oncall note: monitor edge-gw-* queue_len and tenant burst alerts for 48h. I'll add a postmortem template entry if we get a recurrence.

michael: Assigned follow-ups: INFRA-4581 (perm fix), SDK-1229 (backport), and MON-9990 (telemetry alert). We'll update this thread after canary.
